Thanks for the heads-up @cyberprophet! Nice approach with the `node_modules` path parsing — clean and lightweight 👍

Our PR takes a slightly broader approach since the `index.js` collision can also happen with local `file://` plugins (not just npm ones resolved through `node_modules`). For example:

```
file:///project/plugins/alpha/src/index.ts
file:///project/plugins/beta/dist/index.js
```

Both would still resolve to `index` with filename-only fallback. So we added:
- `findPackageName()` — walks up to find the nearest `package.json` name (with a `.opencode` boundary guard)
- A directory heuristic that skips generic dirs like `src/dist/lib/build` to find meaningful names

Definitely some overlap though! Might be worth letting the maintainers decide which trade-off they prefer — minimal and targeted vs. broader coverage. Either way the core `node_modules` case gets fixed 🙂

@rekram1-node @nexxeln: could you please have a look at that PR, since https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/1020 have been already merged.

Good point @guazi04 — the local `file://` collision case (`plugins/alpha/src/index.ts` vs `plugins/beta/dist/index.js`) is a real scenario I hadn't covered.

That said, I intentionally kept #15598 minimal for a couple of reasons:

1. **The `node_modules` case is the silent killer.** Users don't control how `import.meta.resolve` rewrites npm specifiers to `file://` URLs — the collision happens invisibly. Local `file://` plugins are authored directly, so the user has more control over filenames.

2. **`findPackageName()` with fs walks adds runtime I/O** to a hot path (config boot). The `node_modules` path-parsing approach is pure string manipulation — zero fs calls.

3. **Smaller diff = easier review.** The broader fix can always land as a follow-up.

But you're right that both approaches fix the core issue. Happy to let @rekram1-node decide which trade-off fits better — or if a combined approach makes sense.

@thdxr This is a 16-line fix for a bug in `getPluginName()` that has 6 open issues (#8759, #10115, #11159, #12285, #14304, #15591) and 3 competing PRs (#8758, #11161, this one).

**The bug:** `import.meta.resolve` rewrites npm plugin specifiers to `file://…/node_modules/<pkg>/dist/index.js`. Then `getPluginName()` extracts only the filename `"index"`, colliding with any project plugin that also has an `index.ts` entry point. The result: plugins silently disappear at runtime with no error.

**This fix:** parse the package name from `node_modules` paths — pure string manipulation, zero fs I/O, no new dependencies. All CI green (Linux + Windows).

## Confirmed workaround for mise / version managers on macOS

I hit this exact issue with [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) (a polyglot version manager) — `node`, `pnpm`, and other mise-managed tools weren't on PATH in the bash tool.

The root cause is what this issue describes: `bash.ts` uses `spawn(command, {shell})` which Node.js translates to `zsh -c <command>` — a non-interactive, non-login shell that only sources `.zshenv`.

**Workaround**: activate mise in `~/.config/zsh/.zshenv` (or wherever your `.zshenv` lives) so it runs in all shell contexts, not just interactive ones:

```zsh
# ~/.zshenv (or ~/.config/zsh/.zshenv)
# Clear any stale mise state from parent shell before re-activating
unset __MISE_ORIG_PATH MISE_SHELL __MISE_WATCH

eval "$(mise activate zsh)"
```

The `unset` is important: if OpenCode inherits stale mise state vars from the parent shell, mise may skip re-activation thinking it's already done. Clearing them first ensures a clean activation.

### Interesting asymmetry in OpenCode itself

`bash.ts` (bash tool) → `spawn(cmd, {shell: "/bin/zsh"})` → `zsh -c` — **non-login, no init**

`prompt.ts` (`/shell` interactive command) → `spawn(zsh, ["-c", "-l", "<init+cmd>"])` → **login shell with `.zshenv` + `.zshrc` explicitly sourced**

These are intentionally different (bash tool is performance-oriented), but the gap means the bash tool and `/shell` command behave very differently for users with version managers.

The `.zshenv` workaround bridges the gap without needing OpenCode changes — though a proper fix in `bash.ts` (login shell or explicit env capture at startup) would be cleaner.

I agree that the FK hypothesis may not hold -- `CREATE TABLE` with a FK constraint should not fail due to `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` since FK enforcement only applies to DML, not DDL. So something else is going on.

**Key fact: this is deterministic, not transient.** The identical failure occurred on two completely separate machines (Mac Studio M2 Max, MacBook Pro M3 Max) with identical symptoms: 5 migration hashes recorded in `__drizzle_migrations`, but no `workspace` table in `sqlite_master`. This rules out disk issues, sleep/power events, or database locking as the cause.

**What may differ from your test setup:** Both of my databases were **not freshly created**. They accumulated real data over several weeks across versions v1.2.13 through v1.2.15 before hitting v1.2.16. The databases had 9 projects, 44 sessions, 1400+ messages, and 6500+ parts at the time of the failed migration. If you tested with a freshly-created database on v1.2.15 and immediately upgraded, that may explain why you cannot reproduce it.

**Pre-fix database state (from backup):**

`__drizzle_migrations` -- 5 entries, all recorded:
```
hash | created_at
(empty) | 1769552633000  (2026-01-27 22:23:53 UTC)
(empty) | 1770830228000  (2026-02-11 17:17:08 UTC)
(empty) | 1770993676000  (2026-02-13 14:41:16 UTC)
(empty) | 1772134200000  (2026-02-26 19:30:00 UTC)  <-- workspace CREATE TABLE
(empty) | 1772228279000  (2026-02-27 21:37:59 UTC)  <-- session ALTER (workspace_id)
```

Tables present in `sqlite_master` (no `workspace`):
```
__drizzle_migrations, control_account, message, part, permission,
project, session, session_share, team, team_member, team_message,
team_task, todo
```

Note: the `session` table **does** have the `workspace_id` column (migration #5 succeeded -- it was a simple `ALTER TABLE`, no FK involved).

**I can provide the following to help reproduce:**

1. **A sanitized reproduction database** -- I can create a copy with all user data (messages, sessions, parts) stripped out but the schema, migration state, and project stubs preserved. This would let you run the v1.2.17 migration against it and see it fail.

2. **The raw schema metadata** -- the full `sqlite_master` dump and `__drizzle_migrations` contents from the pre-fix backup, which I have included above.

Let me know which would be most helpful.

What I got wrong:
- I initially treated this mostly as retry-signal parsing.

@jlongster you nailed it -- the dev build is the cause.

**Root cause confirmed:** I forked the repo and was developing a `feature/agent-teams` branch locally. I built and ran that dev build against my production database on both machines (Mac Studio and MacBook Pro). This build wrote the workspace migration with timestamp `1772134200000` into `__drizzle_migrations`. When the official v1.2.16 release came with the same migration but timestamp `1772056728000` (earlier), the known Drizzle bug caused it to be skipped -- because a newer timestamp was already recorded.

**Evidence from this machine (MacBook Pro):**

Dev build binary still present:
```
~/git/opencode/packages/opencode/dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/opencode
Built: 2026-03-01 01:02
Version: 0.0.0-feature/agent-teams-202603010001
```

The binary was symlinked into PATH:
```
~/.local/bin/opencode -> ~/git/opencode/packages/opencode/dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/opencode
Symlink created: 2026-03-03 21:07
```

Git repo checkout:
```
~/git/opencode/ @ feature/agent-teams branch
HEAD: 482920354 "fix(agent-teams): align theme tokens + use real LLM model picker"
```

Migration timestamp comparison:
```
Dev build (feature/agent-teams):  1772134200000  (2026-02-26 19:30:00 UTC)
Official release (v1.2.16):      1772056728000  (2026-02-25 21:58:48 UTC)
```

The dev build timestamp is ~21 hours newer. When v1.2.16 ran, Drizzle saw that a migration with a newer timestamp was already recorded and skipped the workspace `CREATE TABLE` -- but the dev build had only recorded the hash, not actually created the table (or created a different version of it that was later dropped).

**Sequence of events:**
1. Ran `feature/agent-teams` dev build -- wrote migration hash with timestamp `1772134200000`
2. Upgraded to official v1.2.16 -- Drizzle skipped workspace migration due to known timestamp bug (newer hash already present)
3. Upgraded to v1.2.17 -- `ALTER TABLE workspace` failed because the table was never created

**Conclusion:** The trigger was running a forked dev build against the same database that the official releases use. However, the underlying issue is the known Drizzle migration timestamp ordering bug -- it silently skips migrations instead of raising an error, which makes this kind of scenario fail in a way that is very hard to diagnose. Any contributor testing a local build will hit this if the migration timestamps diverge.

I will update the issue description to reflect this. Thanks for the quick investigation and the pointer to the Drizzle timestamp bug -- that was the key insight.
